name: Amazon OpenSearch Memory
summary: AWS managed memory for agents: store conversation events, extract memories, and search across sessions. Console, CLI, SDKs and SigV4 API; charges apply per the OpenSearch Service price list.
description: Vendor-affiliated listing (Amazon Web Services). Official developer guide (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/opensearch-service/latest/developerguide/memory.html and the markdown twin /memory.md, both HTTP 200): Amazon OpenSearch Memory is a fully managed memory service for AI agents. Your agent or application sends conversations and data as events; OpenSearch Memory extracts facts, summaries and other details as memories; the agent searches those memories across sessions. You create a space, choose the kinds of memory you want, send events, and search. You don't provision servers or request access to a foundation model. CreateEvent returns when the event is stored; extraction runs afterward in the background. Searches are scoped to one actor. Retention: events 1 to 365 days; memories from 1 day to 10 years, or indefinitely. How it works (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/opensearch-service/latest/developerguide/memory-how-it-works.md, HTTP 200): official access methods are the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI (`aws opensearchmemory`), AWS SDKs (service ID OpenSearchMemory), or the API signed with Signature Version 4 using service name `osm`. Space operations use https://osm.{region}.api.aws; event and memory operations use https://{space-id}.osm.{region}.on.aws. That official Accessing section does not list an MCP server; no mcp_endpoint is recorded. Available Regions listed in that guide: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Europe (Frankfurt). Memory types include SEMANTIC, SUMMARY, and CUSTOM. Getting started (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/opensearch-service/latest/developerguide/memory-getting-started.md, HTTP 200) warns that the tutorial creates resources that incur charges for the space, stored event and memories, and the model calls that extract memories, and points to https://aws.amazon.com/opensearch-service/pricing/ (HTTP 200). The public pricing page lists OpenSearch Memory Extraction line items (including model-specific input and output token prices) in a dynamic widget; those dollar amounts were not copied from the placeholder markup. No AWS account was used and no CLI commands were run. The hosted service is proprietary under AWS terms.

agent_access.notes: No MCP endpoint is listed in the official "Accessing OpenSearch Memory" section (console, AWS CLI, SDKs, or SigV4 API with service name osm). Space endpoint pattern: https://osm.{region}.api.aws; event/memory: https://{space-id}.osm.{region}.on.aws. Auth is AWS IAM / Signature Version 4, not a standalone product API key. No AWS account was used and no CLI or API calls were made. Official getting-started tutorial would incur charges; it was not run. Pricing is on the OpenSearch Service price list.
